summary: Interpreted the stall-route receipt (2e5f37f634834b8197227626ed6d99b7) and folded it into the parent account. The intended condition was reached in all eight trials — the stalled leader stayed in Leader state for every 1ms sample while a different server led at term 3, first seen 345-464ms after the partition, so the cluster really did have two servers believing they led it — yet the queued VerifyLeader never reported success: every endpoint was non-nil ('leadership lost while committing log' in seven trials, 'node is not the leader' in two) at 600-602ms, the moment the store stall released the main loop, and the concurrent Apply failed the same way. Those two error values distinguish trials where the verify had been registered and was answered by the leadership-loss cleanup from trials where it never left the channel, so the lease case was already ready when the loop resumed and leadership was given up before the non-voter's acknowledgement could be counted. The child question is refuted for this model (bound to its fixed experiment), a Fact records the behaviour, and the parent question's gap narrows to a sub-millisecond interleaving rather than closing; the parent's own defect claim is untouched, since the non-voter counting was observed directly in its probe. No execution requested.
